prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Business software subscription pricing (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Plan" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Price" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Minimum seats" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Contract" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Support" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Plan" · longest unbreakable word 75px · one-line width 75px
  col 2: header "Price › List price" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 67px
  col 3: header "Price › Billing terms" · longest unbreakable word 86px · one-line width 490px
  col 4: header "Minimum seats" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 109px
  col 5: header "Contract" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 123px
  col 6: header "Support" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 195px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare six business software subscription plans on headline price, billing terms, minimum seats, contract, and support so a buyer can choose a plan.","reading":"Readers scan down the Plan column and across the short comparison columns; they use List price as the quick numeric anchor, read Billing terms as explanatory prose, and compare Minimum seats, Contract, and Support as procurement constraints.","groups":["Plan is the row identifier and reading anchor.","List price and Billing terms form the Price group, but List price is a short numeric key while Billing terms is explanatory prose.","Minimum seats, Contract, and Support are short constraint/comparison columns that should be scanned together across rows."],"keep_intact":["Plan names such as Enterprise, and the Plan header","List prices such as $12 and numeric minimum-seat values","Contract terms and support-level labels, including their longest words","Headers should not break mid-word; Billing terms especially needs its full label width"],"may_wrap":["Billing terms sentences at spaces","The List price and Minimum seats headers at spaces","Longer Contract and Support phrases at spaces, never inside words"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [96, 88, 224, 87, 90, 134] · table 720×500px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 83, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 1/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [96, 88, 221, 87, 102, 125] · table 720×547px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 83, 83, 83, 83, 83] · column headers wrapped 1/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
